title: Typhoon Dolphin hits China’s east coast, over 1 million evacuated
byline: Typhoon Dolphin, the most ​powerful tropical cyclone to hit China this year, made landfall on the country’s eastern coast on Sunday, bringing torrential rain ‌and strong winds and triggering warnings of flooding and landslides.

title: Sri Lanka can be arbitration partner, not rival to Singapore, says FJ&G de Saram litigation head
byline: Sri Lanka must position itself as a collaborative partner rather than a direct competitor to global dispute resolution hubs like Singapore, leveraging its proactive judiciary to build a seamless regional arbitration ecosystem.

title: Joint Opposition seeks full 12-judge SC bench on 22A petitions
byline: While highlighting that they will file petitions against the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution which seeks to extend the retirement age of judges, the Joint Opposition said today it would call for a bench comprising all 12 judges in the Supreme Court to look into the petition.

title: Air India’s Phuket-Delhi turbulence hit flight captain allegedly failed dope test; suspended
byline: The captain who operated Air India’s turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight on August 4 has reportedly tested positive for psychoactive substances in a post-flight dope test.

title: SLBFE portal opens today for 16,000 Israel job applicants
byline: The Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) will open its online registration portal today (Aug. 10) for Sri Lankans seeking employment in the restaurant and renovation sectors in Israel.

title: Sharp rise in Syphilis cases among men in Sri Lanka
byline: Men account for the majority of reported early syphilis cases in Sri Lanka, with cases among men significantly outnumbering those among women, according to data from the National STD/AIDS Control Programme.

title: Drone operator arrested over Kasikote elephant disruption
byline: Wildlife officials have arrested a person for flying a drone in a manner that obstructed wild elephants travelling along the Galgamuwa–Kasikote main road in the North Western Wildlife Zone.

title: From Ethiopia to the World: What Ethiopian Airline’s rise can teach SriLankan Airlines
byline: Ethiopian Airlines is state-owned and generating US$9.1 billion in annual revenue. SriLankan Airlines is state-owned and still depends on the Treasury. The difference is not ownership. It is execution.

title: Lotus Tower could bloom into South East Asia’s largest Christmas tree
byline: Western Province Governor Hanif Yusoof has pitched turning the 350-metre Lotus Tower into South East Asia’s largest Christmas tree this holiday season, unveiling the idea during the launch of PickMe’s Colombo Connect digital ecosystem at the tower on Wednesday.

title: Gunman fires inside Thai government office as country reels from school shooting
byline: A gunman was arrested after ​firing shots at a local government ‌office on the outskirts of Thailand’s capital on Monday, officials said, just days after a teenager’s killing rampage ​at a school in the same province ​reignited debate over gun control.

title: Trump signals shift to economic pressure on Iran over new military strikes
byline: United States President Donald Trump has said Washington is relying on economic pressure rather than new military strikes to push Iran towards making a deal.

title: Sagara Kariyawasam arrested
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) General Secretary Sagara Kariyawasam was arrested by the Colombo Central Crimes Investigation Bureau (CCIB) a short while ago in connection with an ongoing investigation.

title: Three underworld suspects arrested in Malaysia to be brought back to Sri Lanka
byline: Three individuals suspected of involvement in organized crime, including “Ratmalana Saima,” a key associate of alleged organized crime figure Kanjipani Imran, who were arrested in Malaysia, are scheduled to be brought back to Sri Lanka today under a special security operation.

title: SLPP General Secretary appears before CCIB
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) General Secretary Sagara Kariyawasam appeared before the Colombo Central Crimes Investigation Bureau (CCIB) this morning in connection with an ongoing investigation.

title: Heavy rain pushes Castlereagh, Maussakelle to spill levels
byline: The Castlereagh and Maussakelle reservoirs have risen close to their spill levels following heavy rainfall in their respective catchment areas, engineers in charge of the reservoirs said today (10).

title: Iran ties Hormuz reopening to US concessions on several demands
byline: Iran said it was nearing a final pact with Oman defining new shipping lanes between them through the Strait of Hormuz ​but repeated that the U.S. must meet other conditions, including compensation and an end to sanctions and military threats, before the strategic waterway is reopened.

title: HRCSL summons prison and security officials over recent unrest
byline: The Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka (HRCSL) has summoned senior officials from several key institutions for a special discussion following a series of tense incidents reported at prisons across the country.

title: China, India, Oman eye Mattala Airport
byline: Companies from China and India are among the bidders who have submitted proposals for the operation of the Mattala International Airport, the Daily Mirror learns.

title: Mobile drug-testing bus handed over to NITM
byline: The Health Ministry today handed over a fully equipped mobile drug-testing bus to the National Institute of Transport Medicine (NITM) to strengthen the national programme aimed at detecting drug use among public transport personnel and improving road safety.

title: 2026 Grade Five Scholarship results to be released within a month
byline: The results of the 2026 Grade Five Scholarship Examination will be released within a month, Commissioner General of Examinations Indika Kumari Liyanage said today.

title: Govt. targets teacher shortages in North, East
byline: The Government is to give priority to schools facing teacher shortages, particularly in the Northern and Eastern provinces, while expediting the recruitment of teachers for key subjects such as Science and Mathematics.

title: Strong winds of up to 40 kmph expected in several areas
byline: Strong winds of up to 40 kmph are expected at times over the North Central, North Western, Central and Southern provinces and Trincomalee District, the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Protest in India state intensifies over alleged corruption in job exams
byline: Thousands of protesters in the eastern Indian state of Jharkhand are marching to the state assembly to demand reforms in recruitment exams.

title: Sri Lankan student assumes Presidency of Junior Enterprises Europe
byline: Sri Lankan student Deshabhi Weerawardane has assumed duties as the new President of Junior Enterprises Europe (JE Europe), marking a significant milestone for Sri Lankan youth in international student leadership and entrepreneurship.

title: Court grants interim order to prevent removal of two Lincoln Navigator vehicles
byline: The Court of Appeal has issued an interim order preventing a Sri Lankan company operating under a licence issued by the Board of Investment (BOI) from removing, exporting, shipping, transporting, selling, transferring, alienating, encumbering or otherwise parting with possession, custody or control of two 2024 Lincoln Navigator L Black Label vehicles.

title: Close relative of Kanjipani Imran shot dead in Maligawatte
byline: A close relative of underworld figure Kanjipani Imran was shot dead in Maligawatte a short while ago, Police said.

title: China evacuates one million from homes as massive storm arrives
byline: Chinese authorities have evacuated more than a million people from their homes in eastern China including the financial capital Shanghai, as Typhoon Dolphin made landfall.

title: Navy, STF seize 7,000 foreign cigarettes in Puttalam
byline: A 49-year-old man has been arrested by the Sri Lanka Navy and the Police Special Task Force (STF) with 7,000 foreign cigarettes in Mullipuram, Puttalam.

title: Google Drive is ending Google Photos backup starting August 10
byline: Google has confirmed that its Drive desktop app will stop supporting automatic Google Photos backup starting August 10, 2026. The change means that the users who rely on Drive’s desktop client to sync photos and videos from their computers will no longer see a new media automatically backed up to Google Photos.

title: Sri Lanka ranks 73rd in global English proficiency index
byline: Sri Lanka has been ranked 73rd out of 123 countries and regions in the 2025 EF English Proficiency Index (EF EPI), placing the country in the “Low Proficiency” category.

title: World’s oceans hit record-high July temperatures
byline: The world’s oceans hit their hottest ever recorded temperatures for July, partly fuelled by developing El Niño conditions in the Pacific, according to the EU’s climate monitoring service.

title: Health Ministry warns against misleading reports on firewood use
byline: The Health Ministry has warned that misleading media reports about the use of firewood for cooking could cause unnecessary concerns among the public and create problems in the country’s energy sector.

title: Sri Lanka considers death penalty for drug-related offences
byline: Attention has been drawn to the possibility of imposing the death penalty for drug-related offences during a meeting of the “Ratama Ekata” (Country Together) National Operation Council held at the Presidential Secretariat on Monday (10).

title: 1,506 of 4,962 drug offenders undergoing rehabilitation
byline: Rehabilitation programmes are currently being provided to 1,506 of the 4,962 inmates convicted by courts for drug-related offences, officials told the Sectoral Oversight Committee on Governance, Justice and Civil Protection.

title: ’Body in suitcase’ found in Australia turns out to be lifelike doll
byline: Australian police called in to investigate a body found in a suitcase have concluded that the ’’victim’’ was in fact a lifelike doll.

title: CSE extends winning streak as ASPI rises for fourth straight session
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange began the week on a mixed note on Monday, 10 August 2026, with the All Share Price Index extending its positive momentum for a fourth consecutive session, while the S&P Sri Lanka 20 Index closed marginally lower.

title: Battery storage systems to join national grid in September
byline: Commercial-scale battery energy storage systems being installed at 16 electricity transmission substations across Sri Lanka are expected to be connected to the national grid in early September.

title: Fake SLS helmets: Company fined Rs. 80,000
byline: The Kurunegala Magistrate’s Court has fined a company Rs. 80,000 for manufacturing and selling safety helmets bearing a falsely printed SLS standard logo without obtaining the required certification from the Sri Lanka Standards Institution (SLSI).

title: Sri Lanka’s landmine clearance programme a great success: Rosamund Pike
byline: Award-winning Hollywood actress and International Ambassador for Landmine Clearance Rosamund Pike has described Sri Lanka’s landmine clearance programme as a “great success.”

title: Sagara Kariyawasam released on bail
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) General Secretary Sagara Kariyawasam has been released on bail after being produced before Kaduwela Magistrate Aruna Buddhadasa today.

title: Interpol Red Notice suspect brought back to Sri Lanka from Malaysia
byline: A 41-year-old organized crime suspect Dhanushka Kaushalya alias “Ratmalana Saima,” wanted under an Interpol Red Notice has been arrested in Malaysia and brought back to Sri Lanka, along with two other suspects, following a joint operation involving local and international law enforcement authorities.
